saha.name: Saha-gu
saha.blurb: The southwest, globally known for the colourful hillside maze of Gamcheon Culture Village looking out over the harbour.

gijang.name: Gijang-gun
gijang.blurb: Busan's only rural county, on the northeastern coast -- quiet fishing villages and the seaside Haedong Yonggungsa Temple.

gangseo.name: Gangseo-gu
gangseo.blurb: Busan's largest district by area, spread across the Nakdong River delta -- wetlands, farmland, the Noksan industrial complex, and Gimhae International Airport.

geumjeong.name: Geumjeong-gu
geumjeong.blurb: Up in the northern mountains: Pusan National University's lively student strip, the historic Beomeosa Temple, and the Geumjeong Mountain Fortress.

haeundae.name: Haeundae-gu
haeundae.blurb: Busan's premier tourism and luxury hotspot -- Korea's most famous beach, the high-rises of Marine City, and the convention-and-shopping mass of Centum City.

buk.name: Buk-gu
buk.blurb: A densely populated residential area against the northern ridges, along the lower Nakdong River.

sasang.name: Sasang-gu
sasang.blurb: The western transit and industrial gateway -- riverside green space at Samnak Eco Park along the Nakdong.

busanjin.name: Busanjin-gu
busanjin.blurb: Busan's bustling commercial core. Contains Seomyeon -- the massive central intersection of shopping streets, underground arcades and nightlife -- and the trendy cafe neighbourhood of Jeonpo-dong.

dongnae.name: Dongnae-gu
dongnae.blurb: A historic residential area with traditional roots -- hot-spring spas at Oncheon-dong, and the region's Joseon-era administrative seat.

yeonje.name: Yeonje-gu
yeonje.blurb: The administrative heart -- Busan Metropolitan City Hall is here -- blending quiet residential streets with busy civic and commercial avenues.

nam.name: Nam-gu
nam.blurb: A university and residential zone (Pukyong and Kyungsung universities) with youthful energy that spills toward the coast at Igidae.

yeongdo.name: Yeongdo-gu
yeongdo.blurb: An island district reaching south into the sea. Dramatic coastal cliffs at Taejongdae, maritime history, and the colourful seaside alleys of Huinnyeoul Culture Village.

suyeong.name: Suyeong-gu
suyeong.blurb: Home to Gwangalli Beach and the Gwangan Bridge. Shoreline cafe and pub culture, and big night festivals and drone light shows.

seo.name: Seo-gu
seo.blurb: A coastal residential and medical hub west of the old centre. Songdo Beach with its ocean cable car, and rugged seaside walking trails.

jung.name: Jung-gu
jung.blurb: The historic old downtown by the harbour. Compact but packed with landmarks -- BIFF Square, Jagalchi Fish Market, Gukje Market and Yongdusan Park.

dong.name: Dong-gu
dong.blurb: The city's historic gateway, centred on Busan Station. Steep hillside neighbourhoods, winding staircases, and old-meets-new urban regeneration.

places.name: Beomeosa Temple
places.note: One of Korea's principal Zen temples, on the wooded slopes of Geumjeongsan in the far north of the city. A 7th-century founding with halls tucked among the pines; pairs naturally with a Geumjeongsan hike.

places.name: BIFF Square
places.note: The street-food heart of the Nampo district, named for the Busan International Film Festival. Seed-hotteok pancakes, tteokbokki and gimbap; the trendy Gwangbok shopping street runs right around the corner.

places.name: Duff Cafe
places.note: A 'fever dream from a children's nightmare' cafe in the middle of Gamcheon Culture Village -- a rooftop view over the pastel houses, aggressive ducks to feed downstairs, and a banana-milk coffee. A fun sightseeing pit stop (honourable mention, 60/100, in one cafe ranking).

places.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
places.note: A former Korean-War refugee settlement transformed in 2009 into a hillside labyrinth of pastel houses, murals and hidden street art -- the 'Santorini of Korea.' Free; steep alleys, cafes and viewpoints. Lose an afternoon here.

places.name: Gukje Market
places.note: A sprawling traditional market beside BIFF Square in Nampo -- clothes, tools, imported goods and street food, grown out of post-war informal trading.

places.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
places.note: A rare Korean temple built right on the sea, on the northeastern coast near Gijang. Pass the 12 zodiac statues at the entrance and descend the steps to golden shrines on the cliffs; go early. Free entry -- a taxi or Uber is the easiest way there.

places.name: Haeundae Beach
places.note: Busan's most famous stretch of sand -- soft, white, wide, with a wall of high-rises and hotels behind it. Swimming, seaside walks, lively nights. Free. Also the base for the Sky Capsule and Blue Line Park.

places.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
places.note: A cliffside village on Yeongdo island -- whitewashed lanes strung along the coast with cozy cafes looking straight out to sea. Quieter and more local-feeling than Gamcheon.

places.name: Igidae Coastal Trail
places.note: A cliff-edge coastal walk in Nam-gu on wooden decks and a suspension bridge, looking across the water to the Gwangan Bridge and the Haeundae skyline.

places.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
places.note: South Korea's largest seafood market, on the Nampo waterfront -- run for decades by its women vendors. Choose your catch from the tanks on the ground floor and take it upstairs to be cooked: sashimi, grilled fish, giant octopus.

places.name: Lotte Department Store -- Busan Main
places.note: The flagship Lotte Department Store in Seomyeon -- Busan's downtown, and the transit hub where the two main subway lines cross. All-rounder base area: budget-to-mid hotels, endless restaurants and shopping.
places.geocode_query: Lotte Department Store Busan Main Seomyeon

places.name: Naive Brewers
places.note: A cafe near Jeonpo Cafe Street. The latte arrives with a scoop of ice cream on top that reads as a marshmallow; a travelling duo scored it 76/100, praising the coffee and the not-too-on-the-nose hipster decor. Very small stools.

places.name: Samgwangsa Temple
places.note: A large temple on the western hillside of Busanjin, spectacular during the May lantern festival for Buddha's Birthday when tens of thousands of lanterns fill the courtyards.

places.name: Songdo Bay Cable Car
places.note: The Busan Air Cruise -- a sea cable car gliding from Songdo Bay Station to Amnam Park, standard or glass-floor 'crystal' cabin (~15-20 min). Pair it with the Songdo Cloud Trails, a cliffside skywalk over the surf.

places.name: Suan Coffee
places.note: A striking modern cafe -- 'looks like a spaceship' -- in a quiet residential area by the canal. Cream-cheese-foam coffee, brown-butter pecan shortbread, jazz on the speakers. Scored 78.5/100 in one cafe ranking; 'an adult space.'

places.name: Tide
places.note: A coffee bar built around watching the tide roll in -- everyone sits at the bar. Homemade vanilla-bean iced latte, a rosemary lemonade, an Earl-Grey-fudge 'tea grey' pastry. Vibes rated a flat 10/10.

places.name: Working Holiday
places.note: A cafe right on Haeundae Beach -- a standout croissant and 'the best pasta I've had in Korea' per one review, though the latte 'tastes like melted ice cream.' Herman Miller tables, an IKEA couch, Noguchi-style lamps. Geocoded address is actually Gwangalli (Suyeong-gu), not Haeundae-gu -- v1's own description called it Haeundae Beach; either a different branch exists or the original description was approximate. Confirm before routing.
